layers.name: BASE
layers.effect: Global conditioning/control area for Anima diffusion-side inputs: timestep embeddings and the LLM adapter. It controls denoising schedule behavior, prompt/tag interpretation, concept routing, and adapter-to-DiT conditioning. High-impact and fragile: usually keep fixed unless intentionally transferring prompt-understanding or model-wide conditioning behavior. Qwen/text-encoder tensors are not included because they were not present in the provided checkpoint key list. Anima 2.9B compatibility: the same BASE/LLM-adapter role is retained; the expanded variant adds no separate Planner base-model category.

layers.name: L00
layers.effect: Input/token anchoring stage. Includes x_embedder plus the first DiT block, so it strongly affects latent token formation, coarse local separation, initial edge stability, low-level noise/texture intake, and the earliest image-token structure. Very sensitive for base compatibility. Anima 2.9B note: physical L00 keeps the same normal-Anima source position.

layers.name: L01
layers.effect: Early structure stage. Establishes simple silhouette, coarse local geometry, early body/clothing mass, and basic prompt-conditioned separation. Useful for subtle structure repair but can affect the base image feel if overused. Anima 2.9B note: physical L01 keeps the same normal-Anima source position.

layers.name: L02
layers.effect: Early structure/detail stage. Affects local contours, simple limb/body masses, early character placement, and coarse object separation. Good for low-level shape support rather than identity or finished style. Anima 2.9B note: physical L02 is an inserted expansion layer copied from normal Anima L01; it does not represent normal Anima L02 when the loaded checkpoint is 2.9B.

layers.name: L03
layers.effect: Early layout consolidation. Stabilizes broad geometry, person/object separation, camera/layout anchoring, and the transition from coarse latent structure into more semantic layout. Anima 2.9B note: physical L03 corresponds to normal Anima L02 after the interleaved 28→40 expansion.

layers.name: L04
layers.effect: Early-mid transformer stage. Begins transferring pose tendencies, clothing structure, body orientation, and prompt-to-structure alignment. Useful for light pose/layout inheritance while still mostly preserving late rendering style. Anima 2.9B note: physical L04 corresponds to normal Anima L03 after the interleaved 28→40 expansion.

layers.name: L05
layers.effect: Early-mid structure stage. Useful for body proportions, limb relation, simple interaction geometry, and style-aware shape formation without fully changing the final finish. Anima 2.9B note: physical L05 is an inserted expansion layer copied from normal Anima L03; it does not represent normal Anima L05 when the loaded checkpoint is 2.9B.

layers.name: L06
layers.effect: Early-mid detail routing. Supports clothing complexity, hair/body mass, local structure refinement, and preparation for deeper pose/concept integration. Anima 2.9B note: physical L06 corresponds to normal Anima L04 after the interleaved 28→40 expansion.

layers.name: L07
layers.effect: Early-mid pose/detail bridge. Affects dynamic pose individuality, character placement, body orientation, and scene layout before central blocks perform stronger semantic integration. Anima 2.9B note: physical L07 corresponds to normal Anima L05 after the interleaved 28→40 expansion.

layers.name: L08
layers.effect: Mid structure stage. Stronger effect on pose coherence, character arrangement, perspective, and prompt-conditioned structure than earlier blocks. Good entry point for pose or scenario transfer. Anima 2.9B note: physical L08 is an inserted expansion layer copied from normal Anima L05; it does not represent normal Anima L08 when the loaded checkpoint is 2.9B.

layers.name: L09
layers.effect: Mid structure and concept stage. Useful for prompt-conditioned body/face relation, multi-part consistency, clothing relation, and early character/scenario binding. Anima 2.9B note: physical L09 corresponds to normal Anima L06 after the interleaved 28→40 expansion.

layers.name: L10
layers.effect: Mid integration stage. Balances pose, clothing, face support, identity hints, and concept-conditioned structure. Useful for transferring scenario logic without heavily changing final color. Anima 2.9B note: physical L10 corresponds to normal Anima L07 after the interleaved 28→40 expansion.

layers.name: L11
layers.effect: Mid integration bridge. Good for correcting anatomy/layout and prompt-structure alignment while preserving later rendering style. Often safe for structure-focused merges. Anima 2.9B note: physical L11 is an inserted expansion layer copied from normal Anima L07; it does not represent normal Anima L11 when the loaded checkpoint is 2.9B.

layers.name: L12
layers.effect: Central integration stage. Core block for pose, identity hints, body structure, multi-character relation, and global composition mixing. High value for structural or scenario transfer. Anima 2.9B note: physical L12 corresponds to normal Anima L08 after the interleaved 28→40 expansion.

layers.name: L13
layers.effect: Central concept/style integration. Affects character identity support, expression support, body/face relationship, scene relation, and global composition. Can start to pull style if MLP is strong. Anima 2.9B note: physical L13 corresponds to normal Anima L09 after the interleaved 28→40 expansion.

layers.name: L14
layers.effect: Central detail and structure routing. Useful for clothing/hair detail, hand/body structure, pose consistency, concept stability, and interaction geometry. Anima 2.9B note: physical L14 is an inserted expansion layer copied from normal Anima L09; it does not represent normal Anima L14 when the loaded checkpoint is 2.9B.

layers.name: L15
layers.effect: Central-to-late integration. Bridges structural decisions into local detail and rendering texture. Useful for refined anatomy, expressions, and scenario relation while still carrying broad structure influence. Anima 2.9B note: physical L15 corresponds to normal Anima L10 after the interleaved 28→40 expansion.

layers.name: L16
layers.effect: Late-mid structure/rendering bridge. Strong for refined anatomy, hand/finger placement, facial layout, expression, pose stability, and the first visible style/detail formation. Anima 2.9B note: physical L16 corresponds to normal Anima L11 after the interleaved 28→40 expansion.

layers.name: L17
layers.effect: Late-mid detail integration. Useful for face/body finish, hand/detail cleanup, clothing density, local consistency, and expression/style balance. Anima 2.9B note: physical L17 is an inserted expansion layer copied from normal Anima L11; it does not represent normal Anima L17 when the loaded checkpoint is 2.9B.

layers.name: L18
layers.effect: Late-mid rendering stage. Impacts lighting, detail clarity, texture, facial/hand finish, and local material separation while still carrying structure influence. Anima 2.9B note: physical L18 corresponds to normal Anima L12 after the interleaved 28→40 expansion.

layers.name: L19
layers.effect: Late-mid to late transition. Consolidates local structure, expression, hand/body detail, and style/detail without overhauling early composition as much as later blocks. Anima 2.9B note: physical L19 corresponds to normal Anima L13 after the interleaved 28→40 expansion.

layers.name: L20
layers.effect: Late rendering stage. Strong impact on line quality, color response, lighting, texture, and finished style feel. Use cautiously when preserving the base style. Anima 2.9B note: physical L20 corresponds to normal Anima L14 after the interleaved 28→40 expansion.

layers.name: L21
layers.effect: Late style/detail stage. Useful for painterly finish, hair/clothing texture, material separation, local polish, and style transfer. Anima 2.9B note: physical L21 is an inserted expansion layer copied from normal Anima L14; it does not represent normal Anima L21 when the loaded checkpoint is 2.9B.

layers.name: L22
layers.effect: Late facial/detail finish. Affects eyes/face finish, local texture, high-level style lock, small detail clarity, and rendering consistency. Anima 2.9B note: physical L22 corresponds to normal Anima L15 after the interleaved 28→40 expansion.

layers.name: L23
layers.effect: Late image finish stage. Influences contrast, saturation tendency, detail sharpness, local rendering polish, and final visual density. Anima 2.9B note: physical L23 corresponds to normal Anima L16 after the interleaved 28→40 expansion.

layers.name: L24
layers.effect: Very late finish. Strong effect on final color feel, texture, line confidence, small detail reconstruction, and final style lock. Small values can visibly alter output. Anima 2.9B note: physical L24 is an inserted expansion layer copied from normal Anima L16; it does not represent normal Anima L24 when the loaded checkpoint is 2.9B.

layers.name: L25
layers.effect: Very late rendering lock. Useful for final style transfer, lighting/contrast behavior, high-frequency detail, and output polish, but risky for base-style preservation. Anima 2.9B note: physical L25 corresponds to normal Anima L17 after the interleaved 28→40 expansion.

layers.name: L26
layers.effect: Very late detail and color lock. Strongly affects output polish, saturation/contrast, final local features, and texture finish. Prefer low strengths unless targeting final look. Anima 2.9B note: physical L26 corresponds to normal Anima L18 after the interleaved 28→40 expansion.

layers.name: L27
layers.effect: Final DiT block and output-head area. Strongest late-stage control over final look, color/contrast lock, texture finish, final_layer output behavior, and final latent projection. Very high impact and usually kept low/fixed for structural merges. Anima 2.9B note: physical L27 is an inserted expansion layer copied from normal Anima L18; it does not represent normal Anima L27 when the loaded checkpoint is 2.9B.

layers.name: L28
layers.effect: Anima 2.9B only physical index: L28 corresponds to normal Anima L19 after the interleaved 28→40 expansion. Anima-family transformer block corresponding to original 28-block Anima block 19. In 2.9B this is physical layer L28; legacy 28-block weights are mapped here automatically.

layers.name: L29
layers.effect: Anima 2.9B only physical index: L29 corresponds to normal Anima L20 after the interleaved 28→40 expansion. Anima-family transformer block corresponding to original 28-block Anima block 20. In 2.9B this is physical layer L29; legacy 28-block weights are mapped here automatically.

layers.name: L30
layers.effect: Anima 2.9B only: inserted physical transformer layer L30, copied from normal Anima L20 during 28→40 expansion and initialized with the designated residual output projections zeroed. This layer has no native 28-block Anima counterpart at index L30.

layers.name: L31
layers.effect: Anima 2.9B only physical index: L31 corresponds to normal Anima L21 after the interleaved 28→40 expansion. Anima-family transformer block corresponding to original 28-block Anima block 21. In 2.9B this is physical layer L31; legacy 28-block weights are mapped here automatically.

layers.name: L32
layers.effect: Anima 2.9B only physical index: L32 corresponds to normal Anima L22 after the interleaved 28→40 expansion. Anima-family transformer block corresponding to original 28-block Anima block 22. In 2.9B this is physical layer L32; legacy 28-block weights are mapped here automatically.

layers.name: L33
layers.effect: Anima 2.9B only: inserted physical transformer layer L33, copied from normal Anima L22 during 28→40 expansion and initialized with the designated residual output projections zeroed. This layer has no native 28-block Anima counterpart at index L33.

layers.name: L34
layers.effect: Anima 2.9B only physical index: L34 corresponds to normal Anima L23 after the interleaved 28→40 expansion. Anima-family transformer block corresponding to original 28-block Anima block 23. In 2.9B this is physical layer L34; legacy 28-block weights are mapped here automatically.

layers.name: L35
layers.effect: Anima 2.9B only physical index: L35 corresponds to normal Anima L24 after the interleaved 28→40 expansion. Anima-family transformer block corresponding to original 28-block Anima block 24. In 2.9B this is physical layer L35; legacy 28-block weights are mapped here automatically.

layers.name: L36
layers.effect: Anima 2.9B only: inserted physical transformer layer L36, copied from normal Anima L24 during 28→40 expansion and initialized with the designated residual output projections zeroed. This layer has no native 28-block Anima counterpart at index L36.

layers.name: L37
layers.effect: Anima 2.9B only physical index: L37 corresponds to normal Anima L25 after the interleaved 28→40 expansion. Anima-family transformer block corresponding to original 28-block Anima block 25. In 2.9B this is physical layer L37; legacy 28-block weights are mapped here automatically.

layers.name: L38
layers.effect: Anima 2.9B only physical index: L38 corresponds to normal Anima L26 after the interleaved 28→40 expansion. Anima-family transformer block corresponding to original 28-block Anima block 26. In 2.9B this is physical layer L38; legacy 28-block weights are mapped here automatically.

layers.name: L39
layers.effect: Anima 2.9B only physical index: L39 corresponds to normal Anima L27 after the interleaved 28→40 expansion. Final physical transformer block, corresponding to original Anima block 27, plus final_layer output head. Strong influence on final rendering, color/contrast, detail lock, and latent output projection.

layers.name: VAE
layers.effect: VAE encode/decode layers. Empty here because the provided Anima checkpoint element list did not include VAE tensors. Do not assume VAE merge coverage from this candidate map.

elements.name: t_embedder.1.linear_1
elements.effect: Anima timestep embedding first linear stage. Controls denoising-step conditioning, schedule response, global sampling behavior, and how early/late noise states influence structure. High-impact; usually keep low or fixed unless tuning global denoise behavior.

elements.name: t_embedder.1.linear_2
elements.effect: Anima timestep embedding second linear stage. Finishes timestep conditioning and affects global structure/style timing across the denoising trajectory. High-impact; can change model-wide convergence if mixed strongly.

elements.name: t_embedding_norm
elements.effect: Timestep embedding normalization. Stabilizes global denoising balance, prevents unstable or over-sharp timestep conditioning, and affects CFG/sampler response. Fragile global control element.

elements.name: x_embedder.proj.1
elements.effect: Input latent/image-token projection. Controls initial spatial token formation, local separation, low-level structure anchoring, edge/noise intake, and early texture/color foundation. Strong base-compatibility impact.

elements.name: llm_adapter.embed
elements.effect: LLM adapter input embedding. Bridges text/context features into diffusion-side conditioning and affects prompt-adherence foundations, tag vocabulary entry, and concept availability. Very fragile; usually avoid for ordinary style or anatomy merges.

elements.name: llm_adapter.out_proj
elements.effect: LLM adapter output projection. Final adapter-to-DiT conditioning output; strongly affects prompt integration strength, tag priority, character/concept routing, and global conditioning behavior. Very high risk if overmixed.

elements.name: llm_adapter.norm
elements.effect: LLM adapter final norm. Balances adapter output scale and conditioning stability before it enters the DiT. Can affect overall prompt strength and concept reliability.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.self_attn.q_proj
elements.effect: LLM adapter self-attention query. Determines what text/context relations the adapter attends to, including tag ordering, character-attribute binding, and natural-language relation interpretation.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.self_attn.k_proj
elements.effect: LLM adapter self-attention key. Controls adapter-side context matching and lookup for text tokens/concepts. Affects how reliably related tags or phrases are associated.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.self_attn.v_proj
elements.effect: LLM adapter self-attention value. Carries adapter-side context feature content, including concept and relation information that can later affect image conditioning.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.self_attn.o_proj
elements.effect: LLM adapter self-attention output. Integrates adapter-side context mixing and text relation interpretation; can alter prompt parsing behavior globally.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.self_attn.q_norm
elements.effect: LLM adapter self-attention q norm. Stabilizes adapter token-relation queries and helps prevent over/under-attention to text-token relations.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.self_attn.k_norm
elements.effect: LLM adapter self-attention k norm. Stabilizes adapter matching scale and text-context lookup behavior.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.cross_attn.q_proj
elements.effect: LLM adapter cross-attention query. Routes prompt-conditioned context inside the adapter and affects how external/context features are requested by adapter tokens.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.cross_attn.k_proj
elements.effect: LLM adapter cross-attention key. Controls external context lookup and prompt matching inside the adapter. Important for tag/concept availability and relation matching.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.cross_attn.v_proj
elements.effect: LLM adapter cross-attention value. Injects external context/style/concept content into the adapter representation. Strongly tied to prompt and concept transfer.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.cross_attn.o_proj
elements.effect: LLM adapter cross-attention output. Finishes prompt/context integration inside the adapter and can alter final prompt-conditioning behavior.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.cross_attn.q_norm
elements.effect: LLM adapter cross-attention q norm. Stabilizes prompt-routing queries and balanced conditioning strength in adapter cross attention.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.cross_attn.k_norm
elements.effect: LLM adapter cross-attention k norm. Stabilizes context lookup and prompt matching scale in adapter cross attention.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.mlp.0
elements.effect: LLM adapter MLP first projection. Expands adapter features and transforms text/concept representations; can carry character, style, and relation knowledge. High-risk for broad prompt behavior.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.mlp.2
elements.effect: LLM adapter MLP output projection. Compresses adapter features and finishes conditioning representation; affects concept priority and final adapter semantics.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.norm_self_attn
elements.effect: LLM adapter self-attention norm. Stabilizes self-context processing around adapter self attention and affects text-token relation balance.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.norm_cross_attn
elements.effect: LLM adapter cross-attention norm. Balances prompt/context features before or around adapter cross attention; affects concept routing stability.

elements.name: llm_adapter.blocks.*.norm_mlp
elements.effect: LLM adapter MLP norm. Balances adapter feature transformation and conditioning stability before/around concept MLP processing.

elements.name: self_attn.q_proj
elements.effect: DiT self-attention query. Decides what image-token relations to attend to; strongly affects pose/layout consistency, body-part relation, multi-character separation, and spatial reasoning.

elements.name: self_attn.k_proj
elements.effect: DiT self-attention key. Provides image-token structural matching and spatial lookup; affects how body parts, characters, and objects correspond across the image.

elements.name: self_attn.v_proj
elements.effect: DiT self-attention value. Carries internal image feature content through self attention, including structure material, local detail, and pose/anatomy information.

elements.name: self_attn.output_proj
elements.effect: DiT self-attention output. Integrates self-attention results into the block output; controls structural finish, global consistency, pose cohesion, and multi-part image stability.

elements.name: self_attn.q_norm
elements.effect: DiT self-attention q norm. Stabilizes query strength in self attention and helps control structural balance, anatomy drift, and excessive image-token attention.

elements.name: self_attn.k_norm
elements.effect: DiT self-attention k norm. Stabilizes self-attention matching and helps prevent unstable structure drift, duplicate parts, or weak spatial correspondence.

elements.name: cross_attn.q_proj
elements.effect: DiT cross-attention query. Determines how image tokens request prompt/context information; affects prompt adherence, character/object placement, scenario binding, and tag-controlled structure.

elements.name: cross_attn.k_proj
elements.effect: DiT cross-attention key. Controls text/context lookup and matching for characters, objects, relationships, style tags, and attribute binding.

elements.name: cross_attn.v_proj
elements.effect: DiT cross-attention value. Injects concept/style/content from conditioning into image tokens; affects character traits, clothing, expression cues, object details, and style content.

elements.name: cross_attn.output_proj
elements.effect: DiT cross-attention output. Integrates prompt/context information into the image stream; affects final prompt adherence, concept finish, style transfer, and scenario coherence.

elements.name: cross_attn.q_norm
elements.effect: DiT cross-attention q norm. Stabilizes prompt-routing strength from image tokens and helps balance under/over-adherence to conditioning.

elements.name: cross_attn.k_norm
elements.effect: DiT cross-attention k norm. Stabilizes context lookup and prompt matching scale; useful for reducing unstable tag mixing or weak concept binding.

elements.name: mlp.layer1
elements.effect: DiT MLP first projection. Expands per-token features; affects drawing density, shape refinement, face/hand/clothing detail, material texture, and style/detail formation.

elements.name: mlp.layer2
elements.effect: DiT MLP second projection. Compresses and returns transformed features; affects detail finish, rendering consolidation, local polish, style output, and color/texture expression.

elements.name: adaln_modulation_self_attn.1
elements.effect: AdaLN modulation for self-attention first stage. Timestep/conditioning modulation over internal structure and pose; affects how strongly self-attention participates at each denoise phase.

elements.name: adaln_modulation_self_attn.2
elements.effect: AdaLN modulation for self-attention second stage. Self-attention gating and denoising-step balance; useful for controlling pose/anatomy influence without directly replacing attention weights.

elements.name: adaln_modulation_cross_attn.1
elements.effect: AdaLN modulation for cross-attention first stage. Timestep/conditioning modulation over prompt-conditioning strength and concept routing balance.

elements.name: adaln_modulation_cross_attn.2
elements.effect: AdaLN modulation for cross-attention second stage. Cross-attention gating and prompt/style influence; affects how strongly prompt concepts enter image tokens across denoising.

elements.name: adaln_modulation_mlp.1
elements.effect: AdaLN modulation for MLP first stage. Controls feature expansion balance for density, lighting, material expression, and style/detail growth over denoising.

elements.name: adaln_modulation_mlp.2
elements.effect: AdaLN modulation for MLP second stage. MLP gating and rendering finish; affects style/detail strength, polish, and late-stage texture consolidation.

elements.name: final_layer.adaln_modulation.1
elements.effect: Final-layer AdaLN modulation first stage. Final denoising/output conditioning and image-head balance; affects output-head response, color/contrast tendency, and final structural projection.

elements.name: final_layer.adaln_modulation.2
elements.effect: Final-layer AdaLN modulation second stage. Final output gating and last-stage image look lock; high-impact for final style/color/detail behavior.

elements.name: final_layer.linear
elements.effect: Final linear image head. Final latent-to-output projection; strongly affects final color/contrast lock, texture finish, output sharpness, and visible image structure. Very sensitive.

elements.name: pos_embedder.dim_spatial_range
elements.effect: Anima 2.9B candidate addition: spatial positional-range control present in the supplied 2.9B key set. It affects spatial coordinate scaling/geometry behavior and should be changed conservatively when preserving normal-Anima behavior.

elements.name: pos_embedder.dim_temporal_range
elements.effect: Anima 2.9B candidate addition: temporal positional-range control present in the supplied 2.9B key set. For still-image merging it is a global/fragile positional-control element and is usually kept near the base.

elements.name: pos_embedder.seq
elements.effect: Anima 2.9B candidate addition: positional embedding sequence tensor present in the supplied 2.9B key set. It influences global spatial positional organization and is best treated as a conservative BASE-level element.

mode_notes.Checkpoint: Use these as guidance when designing Anima checkpoint merge elemental ratios. For SIM/AD-style merges, use alpha mainly as difference-injection amount and beta as a similarity/stability gate. L00-L07 bias input/early structure and coarse layout; L08-L15 are the safest core range for pose, scenario relation, prompt-structure binding, and multi-character composition; L16-L19 refine face, expression, hands, anatomy, clothing, and local structure; L20-L27 strongly influence final rendering, style, color, lighting, contrast, and detail lock. BASE/llm_adapter, t_embedder, x_embedder, and final_layer are high-impact global areas and should usually be fixed or used at very low strength unless intentionally changing conditioning or output-head behavior.
mode_notes.LoRA: For Anima LoRA bake, use narrow attention/MLP/AdaLN targets when preserving the base. self_attn is best for pose, layout, anatomy, and multi-character separation; cross_attn is best for prompt adherence, characters, clothing, objects, and scenario concepts; mlp is best for face/hand/clothing detail, texture, rendering density, color, and style; AdaLN modulation changes when/how strongly those paths act during denoising. Avoid or minimize llm_adapter unless the LoRA intentionally trains prompt-understanding/knowledge behavior. Late L20-L27 and final_layer targets strongly affect finish and color.
mode_notes.LyCORIS: LyCORIS can target the same logical elements. Per-layer validity matters: BASE contains timestep and adapter elements, L00-L27 contain DiT block elements, L00 additionally has x_embedder, and L27 additionally has final_layer elements. For base preservation, prefer central self_attn/cross_attn/AdaLN subsets over broad all-layer MLP or final_layer targeting. For style transfer, prefer L16-L27 MLP/AdaLN_MLP with cautious late-block strength.

variant_notes.Anima: Primary/default candidate semantics are the normal 28-block Anima catalog. L00-L27 aliases/effects and Checkpoint/LoRA/LyCORIS applicability remain the baseline.
variant_notes.Anima 2.9B: Compatibility extension of the same Anima base model. Physical blocks are expanded from 28 to 40 with insertions at L02, L05, L08, L11, L14, L17, L21, L24, L27, L30, L33, and L36. Items explicitly labeled “Anima 2.9B candidate addition” or “Anima 2.9B only” are additions to the normal-Anima candidate baseline.
